newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem Algeria rebels kill 36, blast rocks Algiers.
newsitem.headline: Moslem Algeria rebels kill 36, blast rocks Algiers.

text.p: Moslem rebels in Algeria killed 36 people overnight in a village, Algerian security forces said, and Algiers residents said a huge blast rocked the capital on Sunday evening.
"We heard a huge explosion 20 minutes ago in the centre of the capital but we do not know yet exactly where," said one resident speaking by telephone from Algiers.

Earlier the security forces said in a statement carried by the official Algerian news agency APS that 36 people were killed in Sidi Abdelaziz village in Medea province, a Moslem guerrilla stronghold, 70 km (40 miles) south of Algiers.
The killing was the worst in a series of massacres, mostly in remote villages, and bombings in Algiers and surrounding towns in which more than 300 people have died in the past two-and-a-half months.
They blamed the massacre on a "group of terrorists", the term the authorities use to describe Moslem guerrillas in Algeria.
On Thursday a powerful bomb ripped through a crowded car market in Boufarik, a town 30 km (20 miles) south of Algiers, on Thursday, killing 14 people and wounding about 100.
Two car bombs killed 20 people early this month in Algiers and the eastern town of Ain-Fakroun.
Moslem guerrillas killed 14 villagers seven days ago in Tabinat hamlet in Blida province, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.
Guerrillas kidnapped and slit the throats of five girls in the same day in the neighbouring Haouch Enlgise village.
The highest death toll in the recent series of attacks before the Sidi Abdelaziz massacre was on November 6 when the guerrillas killed 31 villagers in Sidi el Kebir, near the garrison town of Blida.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
